purpose: Compare the frozen reader and the Veritas reader through Shadow.consume, including policy evaluation, observation and decision journaling, follow-up processing, and periodic saves, using an isolated temporary journal and identical finalized public source records.

method.clock_model: Both time.monotonic() and time.monotonic_ns() follow the recorded monotonic clock, initialized from the saved context clock; time.time_ns() follows recorded receipt time.
method.journal: Fresh temporary SQLite journal for each pass; source, campaign, and persisted runtime inputs read-only.

verification.peak_rss_reader_smoke_check: /proc/self/status VmHWM reader returned 159490048 bytes; peak-RSS comparison omitted from A/B results because an earlier resource.getrusage conversion disagreed with the cgroup measurement.

limitations: This is one bounded 16-segment historical replay per implementation, not a live-worker catch-up measurement or long-run throughput distribution.
The range starts from a saved mid-campaign runtime cursor; it validates exact normalized decision, commitment, and follow-up rows for the compared range only.
The replay produced no new market discovery or economic finding. Its 12 observed and 500 censored follow-up rows reproduce the existing saved runtime labels.
The code remains in project/veritas and is not deployed to, or used to restart, the protected Reality worker.
The process peak-RSS field is excluded from comparative results because the prior getrusage-based value conflicted with the scope memory peak; the benchmark runner now reads Linux VmHWM directly.
decision: Retain the reader optimization in the branch. Its bounded full-consume replay is state- and research-row-equivalent with materially lower CPU on this range. Keep the protected frozen campaign unchanged; assess any future deployment only through the authorized campaign lifecycle and a separate acceptance review.
